title: Baghel Singh Withdraws and Begins the Delhi Shrines

blocks.text: Once terms are struck, the Delhi ruler sent a message to S. Baghel Singh asking that the Khalsa be drawn back from immediate plunder. Baghel Singh manages the withdrawal in an orderly way while still warning the Panth about imperial concentration and the danger of fresh alliances against them.

The retreat is therefore strategic rather than submissive. After the Khalsa Dal beat a hasty retreat from the edge of Delhi, Baghel Singh put up his camp at Subzi Mandi and begins operating from a position that still commands respect.

From there the narrative turns constructive. Revenues and honors are acknowledged, and Baghel Singh started construction of Sikh shrines so that political leverage in Delhi is translated into lasting sacred presence.
